newsitem.title: ECUADOR: PETROECUADOR GIVES GO-AHEAD TO PIPELINE EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: PETROECUADOR GIVES GO-AHEAD TO PIPELINE EXPANSION.

text.p: The board of Ecuadorean state oil company Petroecuador has given the go-head for construction work to begin on the expansion of the Transecuadorean oil pipeline, said a Petroecuador source Thursday.
"The board met Wednesday night and approved the start of construction work," said the company official, who asked not to be named.

The Petroecuador board includes the energy, industry and finance ministers, the head of the armed forces joint command, a worker representative, an aide of the president and a member of the National Development Council.
The expansion work is expected to increase the pipeline's crude transport capacity to 410,000 bpd from 340,000 bpd. It is expected to cost about $80 million.

The project will be 90-percent financed by a group of foreign oil companies comprised of U.S. firms City Investing, Oryx and Arco and the Argentine oil company YPF, as well as Ecuador's Tripetrol. (( Maria Veronica Barreiros, Quito Newsroom 5932 2584333 ext.116 e-mail:reuters1@reutersecu.com.ec))
